text:
kai: morning brainstorm 1. idea: micro-lane + groomer pattern. separate tiny fastpath (micro-lane) that serves <40-token requests with a soft quota and an elastic-groomer that re-batches leftover requests back into the coalescer when helpful. goal: tighten p99 for chatty flows without blowing batch efficiency.

maria: micro-lane how is it different from previous proposals?

kai: two differences: 1) soft quotas per-tenant (not hard FIFO steals). 2) groomer is an async background thread that opportunistically moves queued tiny requests into bulk batches when GPU utilization dips, avoiding immediate preemption.

tj: soft quotas sound safer but can still create admission storms. how do we avoid herd/backpressure amplifications?

kai: quotas are token-based and decay over time. plus we add a randomized jitter to admission decisions and rate-limit tenant reclaim attempts.

anya: cache effects again. micro requests might be very prefixy and hurt kvcache hit-rate. can groomer do ordering to colocate similar prefixes?

lee: we could add a cheap locality hint to requests (prefix-hash mod N) and groomer attempts to pack same-hint into batches first. not perfect but lowers kv churn.

sam: what about latency SLOs for the micro-lane itself? need bounded wait + graceful degradation.

kai: micro-lane slot TTL is low (e.g., 40ms), then groomer either reassigns to bulk or marks request degraded and streams a degraded-response header. degrade path avoids retry storms.

maria: eviction semantics: when groomer pulls into bulk pool, how do we handle headroom accounting? we must not exceed batch_token limits.

kai: groomer uses a weighted packing algorithm: it maintains a running token_budget that mirrors bulk_coalesce.max_batch_tokens minus a safety headroom. it only packs up to that budget and triggers immediate backpressure to tiny lane if budget goes negative.

tj: sounds complex. need clear invariants. propose a small state machine doc + unit tests that assert: (a) micro-lane never preempts bulk in normal mode, (b) groomer respects token_budget, (c) kv_miss delta tracked.

lee: telemetry wishlist: micro_lane.enqueue_rate, micro_lane.p50/p95/p99, groomer.pack_efficiency, groomer.pk_token_util, kvcache_miss_by_lane, batch_fill_ratio, gpu_util_pct. set alerts on micro_lane.p99 regressions and pack_efficiency < 0.7.

anya: rollout proposal: feature-flag "micro_lane_groomer_v1". staged rollout: dev -> staging (full synthetic trace) -> 2% canary -> 20% -> 100%. collect p99/p995 and cost-per-token.

sam: failure modes: 1) runaway micro-lane that starves model throughput, 2) groomer bug that packs oversized batches and OOMs. mitigation: watchdog on pack size and autosafety to disable groomer if GPU OOMs spike.

ops-bot: infra note: ensure we register new feature-flag and a kill-switch in deploy.

kai: config sketch: 
```
micro_lane:
  token_threshold: 40
  slot_ttl_ms: 40
  soft_quota_tokens_per_tenant: 256
  quota_decay_ms: 1000
  admission_jitter_ms: 5
  degrade_marker: "X-Redwood-Degraded: micro-lane"
groomer:
  interval_ms: 10
  max_pack_tokens: 4096
  pack_headroom_tokens: 512
  locality_buckets: 16
  pack_efficiency_target: 0.75
routing:
  util_floor_pct: 68
  util_ceiling_pct: 92
  hysteresis_ms: 500
```

maria: docs: expose soft_quota and quota_decay, warn about bursty tenants. also a recommended default for locality_buckets per model family.

tj: tests: unit test state machine, fuzz test groomer packing with skewed prefix distributions, integration with kvcache sim.

lee: monitoring: dashboards + an automated experiment suite that runs daily to detect regressions in pack_efficiency and kv_miss_by_lane.

anya: one more thought: allow customers to opt-out of micro-lane (per-tenant flag) if they need consistent batch economics. docs should show tradeoffs.

kai: next actions: I'll prototype groomer in the local runner, wire metrics, and post an RFC PR with sims and plots. tagging @maria @tj @lee for review.

maria: SGTM. include cost delta and tail percentiles.

tj: will review once PR is up. leave a pointer to test harness.

ops-bot: runbook reminder: add rollback steps and OOM escalation for "micro_lane_groomer_v1".
